$comment: types/database.ts is generated from the live schema and is authoritative for tables, columns,
types, nullability, defaults, enums, functions and foreign keys. It carries NOTHING about
unique constraints, check constraints, partial indexes or RLS policies — Postgres has them,
the generated types don't. That is what this file supplies.
So: never edit column facts here (the generator ignores them). Do update this file in the same
commit as any migration that adds or changes a constraint, index or policy. The generator warns
loudly and marks the HTML when a table in types/database.ts has no entry here.

recipes.purpose: One recipe. The only table with no foreign key — everything else hangs off it.
indexes: recipes_published_created_at_idx on (published, created_at desc) — serves the public list: filter to published, newest first
notes: updated_at is maintained by a trigger, not by the app.
slug is derived from the title and never editable — a rename changes a live URL.

recipe_steps.purpose: Ordered instructions for one recipe. Rewritten wholesale by save_recipe() on every save.
constraints: foreign key (recipe_id) references recipes (id) on delete cascade
notes: image_path is live: one optional photo per step, written by save_recipe() from the steps array. It holds a path inside the recipe-images bucket, not a URL — the project id and CDN host stay out of the database, so the rows survive a project move. See docs/image-storage.md.

recipe_ingredients.purpose: Ordered ingredients for one recipe. Rewritten wholesale by save_recipe() on every save.
constraints: foreign key (recipe_id) references recipes (id) on delete cascade
notes: group_label existed briefly and was removed in c2c231d (2026-08-01) — ingredient grouping is not a feature.

recipe_images.purpose: Gallery images for one recipe. Rewritten wholesale by save_recipe() on every save, like the other two children — even though the wizard sends exactly one row, flagged primary. The many-row shape is what makes a gallery a UI change later rather than a payload change.
constraints: foreign key (recipe_id) references recipes (id) on delete cascade
indexes: recipe_images_one_primary_idx — unique on (recipe_id) where is_primary: unlimited images per recipe, at most one primary
notes: save_recipe() writes this table as of 20260808140818_save_recipe_images.sql — delete-then-insert of the whole set with ordinality, the same treatment steps and ingredients get. That is what retired the collision worry in issue 1 of docs/known-issues.md:13: positions come from array order and the old rows are gone before the new ones land, so the non-deferrable unique (recipe_id, sort_order) never fires. Only a gallery editor that patched rows in place — which nothing does — would still hit it.
storage_path holds a path inside the recipe-images bucket, not a URL, so the project id and CDN host stay out of the database. docs/image-storage.md.

on delete cascade removes these rows but NOT the files they name — Postgres has no idea the bucket exists. deleteRecipe reads the paths BEFORE the row delete for exactly that reason; docs/image-storage.md:98 explains which way each half-failure has to fall.
There is no alt column — dropped in 20260808140817_recipe_images_drop_alt.sql because both placements pass alt="" and a column carrying null forever reads like a bug. Do not add it back for symmetry.

⚠ A row with is_primary false renders nowhere: getRecipes() filters the embed on is_primary, so the file exists, the row exists, and no surface shows either. Nothing raises. Safe today because save_recipe() is only ever handed one image and the wizard always flags it.

rls.summary: Enabled on all four public tables AND on storage.objects — Storage is a second policy surface, and the table model below stops at the table boundary. Two roles either way: visitor (anon) and admin (authenticated), every logged-in account being an admin. anon is granted nothing on storage.objects because rendering never touches it: a public bucket serves object bytes over /object/public/…. The select policy there is required rather than defensive, and this was probed rather than reasoned — storage-api runs the user-facing delete as the caller, with a where clause and `returning`, so with no select policy the delete affects zero rows and still reports success (docs/image-storage.md:119). The recipe-images bucket ROW (public, file_size_limit 2097152, allowed_mime_types {image/webp}, created by 20260808140816_recipe_images_storage.sql) is deliberately absent from the table below: it is data in storage.buckets, so no diff engine sees it and it has to be checked by hand — issue 5 of docs/known-issues.md:138. Full model: docs/permission-model.md; the Storage half: docs/image-storage.md.
grants: grant select on <all four> to anon, authenticated
grant insert, update, delete on <all four> to authenticated
storage.objects carries no grant of ours — Supabase's own storage setup grants the API roles, so the four policies below are the whole of what this project controls there

save_recipe.summary: The only write path for a recipe and its children.
save_recipe.security: security invoker · set search_path = '' · execute revoked from public and anon, granted to authenticated
notes: Exists because Supabase JS sends every statement as its own transaction, so a delete-then-insert of children could leave a recipe with no steps.

Writes all three children — recipe_steps, recipe_ingredients and recipe_images — as whole sets, taking position from array order via `with ordinality`. Delete-then-insert, which is also why the non-deferrable unique constraints on the ordering columns never fire.
Deleting recipe_images rows does not delete the files they name, so replacing a cover through this function orphans the old object. Accepted, and recorded as issue 4 of docs/known-issues.md:104.
Extend it by reading another key off the payload, never by adding parameters.
